historical_references.reference: Saint Cassian of Imola, also known as Cassian the Confessor, was a bishop and a Confessor of the faith in the 5th century. He was born in the Roman province of Emilia, and was the bishop of Imola for about 15 years. During his episcopate, he was known for his holiness and his opposition to the invading Ostrogoths led by King Theodoric. He was martyred in 473 AD during the siege of Imola.
historical_references.context: Bishop and Confessor in Emilia, Italy, during the Ostrogoth invasion

historical_references.reference: Saint Cassian of Marseille, also known as John Cassian, was a monk and a writer in the 5th century. He was born in Constantine, in present day Romania, but studied and taught in Marseille, France. He is best known for his works on monasticism, particularly his Institutes and Conferences, which influenced the Rule of Saint Benedict and the development of Western monasticism.
historical_references.context: Monk and Writer in Marseille, France, known for his works on monasticism
